name: TN-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+13 district lean combined with a Republican-favorable national environment
Garrett's roughly 27-to-1 fundraising edge over Croley, plus outside support on his side
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 4 percent
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot adds modest uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's R+13 lean, a Republican-tilted environment, and Garrett's roughly $2.8 million to $104,000 fundraising advantage all point the same direction, and markets give Croley only about a 4 percent chance. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict those signals, the open seat stays in the Likely Republican column.
model.watch: A surge of Democratic outside spending or any polling showing Croley within single digits would suggest the environment is shifting faster than the district's fundamentals imply.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: John Rose (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Tennessee's 6th District is an open seat after John Rose stepped aside to run for governor, but the Republican hold on this R+13 district shows little sign of loosening. The evidence points firmly to the GOP: the district's partisan lean, a national climate that has favored Republicans, and a large financial gap. Johnny Garrett has raised about $2.8 million and drawn outside support, while Democrat Mike Croley has raised roughly $104,000 with no recorded outside help. Prediction markets give the Democrat only about a 4 percent chance.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on the district's lean, the money race, and market pricing, all of which align. The lack of an incumbent adds some uncertainty, but the structural Republican advantage here is large enough that a Democratic upset would require a major shift in the political environment.
